title: The FIRE Movement: Principles of Financial Independence
content:
The Financial Independence, Retire Early (FIRE) movement is a lifestyle philosophy centered around aggressive savings, low-cost index investing, and deliberate spending to achieve financial freedom decades before traditional retirement age.

The core formula of FIRE revolves around savings rate—the percentage of net income an individual saves and invests each month. While typical households save 5% to 10% of their earnings, FIRE adherents routinely target savings rates of 40%, 50%, or even 70%. A high savings rate works doubly: it dramatically speeds up portfolio accumulation while simultaneously accustoming the individual to living on a smaller budget.

FIRE practitioners calculate their 'FI Number' by multiplying their annual living expenses by 25 (based on the 4% safe withdrawal rate). Once invested assets reach this milestone, passive returns can theoretically support living costs perpetually.

Over time, several FIRE variations have emerged to accommodate diverse lifestyle preferences:
- Lean FIRE: Achieving independence on a minimalist budget, typically under $40,000 annually.
- Fat FIRE: Achieving independence with an abundant budget, typically $100,000+ annually, allowing luxury travel and dining.
- Coast FIRE: Front-loading retirement investments in one's 20s so compound growth will reach the retirement target without any additional contributions, allowing the individual to take lower-stress jobs just to cover current living expenses.
- Barista FIRE: Accumulating partial independence, where passive investments cover basic living costs while part-time work provides health insurance and supplementary cash.
